## D. Spouses Gloria and Efren Balane; Spouses Jomil and Princess Balane Torralba

**Jurisdiction (as instructed, with a record correction).**

- **Gloria, Efren and Jomil** are private individuals on the record.
  - The CSC's disciplinary rules cover government personnel (2017 RACCS §2 "Coverage", via csc.gov.ph search excerpt [VERIFY]).
  - The Ombudsman's disciplinary authority runs to "elective and appointive officials of the Government" (RA 6770 §21).
  - Private persons are reached only "In all cases of conspiracy between an officer or employee of the government and a private person" (RA 6770 §22).
  - No conspiracy fact with a public officer is in the record (see A). **Neither the CSC nor the Ombudsman has jurisdiction over them on this record.**
- **Princess** states that she is an elected Municipal Councilor (JA-P p.4 S19), so she is not a private individual. However:
  - none of her acts in the record relates to her office (survey money, 2006 and later: JA-P S8–S10; residence: S5–S6);
  - the CSC does not discipline elective officials [VERIFY: LGC rules on elective officials were not read];
  - the Ombudsman's §20 exceptions and the §16 tenure rule would apply.
  - **Treat as civil-only on this record.**
- **Gloria** was Kagawad 1997–2004 and Konsehal 2004–2017 (JA-G p.11 S59), and the deed is dated 29 Sep 2016, during her term.
  - Any SALN question for 2016–2017 (RA 6713 §8(A)(a)) is outside the record (no SALN in evidence).
  - It is beyond RA 6770 §20(5)'s one-year period and post-separation.
  - Per Jonathan, Gloria's citizenship is LOW, credibility only.
  - **Treat as civil-only.**
